chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, from Al-Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'O Mufazzal! Listen to what I say to you, and know that it is the truth, and act upon it, and inform your brothers of the 'high standing' (Ilyat). I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what is the high standing of my brothers?' He said: 'Those who are eager to fulfill the needs of their brothers.'

He said, then he said: 'And whoever fulfills a need for his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will fulfill for him on the Day of Resurrection a hundred thousand needs. From those, the first is Paradise, and from them is that He will admit his relatives, his acquaintances, and his brothers into Paradise, after they are not Nasibi (disbelievers in the Imams).'
And it was so that whenever Al-Mufazzal asked a brother from his brothers for a need, he would say to him, 'Do you not desire that you be among the high-standing brothers?'

key_terms.أَوَّلُهَا: The first of them (referring to the fulfilled needs)
key_terms.عِلْيَة: High social standing or elevated status
key_terms.نُصَّاب: Nasibi (one who is hostile to the Imams, specifically in Shia context)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for fulfilling the needs of a fellow believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates fulfilling the needs of believers to a defining characteristic of the 'high standing' (Ilyat) among the community, linking social solidarity directly to eschatological reward. The promise of Allah fulfilling a hundred thousand needs—including the intercession for one's kin to enter Paradise—underscores the transformative power of mutual aid in Shia spiritual ethics. This concept reinforces the communal bond (Ukhuwwah) as a means of purifying the believer's status and securing divine favor on the Day of Judgment.
